rationale: Keeps the comparison, self-giving life, and friendship.
before: No one has greater love than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.
after: No one has greater love than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.
tsw_comparator: Greater love than this no one has, that someone should lay down his life for his friends.
exact_source_record: μείζονα ταύτης ἀγάπην οὐδεὶς ἔχει, ἵνα τις τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ θῇ ὑπὲρ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ.

rationale: Preserves friendship’s condition in obedience.
before: You are my friends if you do what I command you.
after: You are my friends if you do what I command you.
tsw_comparator: You are my friends if you do what I command you.
exact_source_record: ὑμεῖς φίλοι μού ἐστε ἐὰν ποιῆτε ⸀ἃ ἐγὼ ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν.

rationale: Keeps the slave-friend contrast, differing knowledge, and revelation received from the Father.
before: I no longer call you slaves, because a slave does not know what the master is doing. I have called you friends because I have made known to you everything I heard from my Father.
after: I no longer call you slaves, because a slave does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything I heard from my Father.
tsw_comparator: No longer do I call you servants, because the servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, because everything that I heard from my Father I have made known to you.
exact_source_record: οὐκέτι ⸂λέγω ὑμᾶς⸃ δούλους, ὅτι ὁ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν τί ποιεῖ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος· ὑμᾶς δὲ εἴρηκα φίλους, ὅτι πάντα ἃ ἤκουσα παρὰ τοῦ πατρός μου ἐγνώρισα ὑμῖν.

rationale: Preserves initiative, appointment, movement, lasting fruit, and purpose tied to prayer.
before: You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that remains—so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.
after: You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain—so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.
tsw_comparator: You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you so that you might go and bear fruit and that your fruit might remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give to you.
exact_source_record: οὐχ ὑμεῖς με ἐξελέξασθε, ἀλλʼ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔθηκα ὑμᾶς ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑπάγητε καὶ καρπὸν φέρητε καὶ ὁ καρπὸς ὑμῶν μένῃ, ἵνα ὅ τι ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δῷ ὑμῖν.

rationale: Keeps the plural instructions and mutual-love purpose.
before: These things I command you so that you love one another.
after: I command you these things so that you may love one another.
tsw_comparator: These things I command you, so that you may love one another.
exact_source_record: ταῦτα ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους.

rationale: Preserves condition and Jesus’ prior experience of the world’s hatred.
before: “If the world hates you, know that it hated me before it hated you.
after: If the world hates you, know that it hated me before it hated you.
tsw_comparator: If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before you.
exact_source_record: Εἰ ὁ κόσμος ὑμᾶς μισεῖ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐμὲ πρῶτον ⸀ὑμῶν μεμίσηκεν.

rationale: Keeps belonging, possessive love, election out of the world, and resulting hatred.
before: If you were from the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not from the world—rather, I chose you out of the world—the world hates you.
after: If you belonged to the world, the world would love its own. But because you do not belong to the world—instead, I chose you out of the world—the world hates you.
tsw_comparator: If you were of the world, the world would love its own; but because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
exact_source_record: εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἦτε, ὁ κόσμος ἂν τὸ ἴδιον ἐφίλει· ὅτι δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ ἐστέ, ἀλλʼ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, διὰ τοῦτο μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος.

rationale: Preserves the remembered saying and both parallel conditions without forcing the second into irony.
before: Remember the word I told you: ‘A slave is not greater than the master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
after: Remember the word I told you: ‘A slave is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
tsw_comparator: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
exact_source_record: μνημονεύετε τοῦ λόγου οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν· Οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ· εἰ ἐμὲ ἐδίωξαν, καὶ ὑμᾶς διώξουσιν· εἰ τὸν λόγον μου ἐτήρησαν, καὶ τὸν ὑμέτερον τηρήσουσιν.

rationale: Keeps the causal links to Jesus’ name and ignorance of the sender.
before: But they will do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
after: But they will do all these things to you because of my name, since they do not know the one who sent me.
tsw_comparator: But all these things they will do to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
exact_source_record: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα πάντα ποιήσουσιν ⸂εἰς ὑμᾶς⸃ διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τὸν πέμψαντά με.

rationale: Preserves the counterfactual, culpability, present lack of pretext, and repeated sin.
before: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
after: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
tsw_comparator: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
exact_source_record: εἰ μὴ ἦλθον καὶ ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς, ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ⸀εἴχοσαν· νῦν δὲ πρόφασιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

rationale: Keeps the inseparable hatred of Son and Father.
before: Whoever hates me hates my Father also.
after: Whoever hates me also hates my Father.
tsw_comparator: The one hating me also hates my Father.
exact_source_record: ὁ ἐμὲ μισῶν καὶ τὸν πατέρα μου μισεῖ.

rationale: Preserves unique works, counterfactual guilt, sight, and doubled hatred.
before: If I had not done among them the works no one else did, they would not have sin. But now they have seen and hated both me and my Father.
after: If I had not done among them the works no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have seen and hated both me and my Father.
tsw_comparator: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.
exact_source_record: εἰ τὰ ἔργα μὴ ἐποίησα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἃ οὐδεὶς ἄλλος ⸀ἐποίησεν, ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ⸀εἴχοσαν· νῦν δὲ καὶ ἑωράκασιν καὶ μεμισήκασιν καὶ ἐμὲ καὶ τὸν πατέρα μου.

rationale: Keeps fulfillment, their Law, and groundless hatred.
before: But this happened so that the word written in their Law might be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’
after: But this happened so that the word written in their Law might be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’
tsw_comparator: But this is to fulfill the word written in their Law: ‘They hated me without cause.’
exact_source_record: ἀλλʼ ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὁ ⸂ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αὐτῶν γεγραμμένος⸃ ὅτι Ἐμίσησάν με δωρεάν.

rationale: Preserves Advocate and Spirit titles, Jesus’ sending, origin from the Father, procession, and testimony.
before: “When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who goes out from the Father—he will testify about me.
after: When the Advocate comes—the one I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—he will testify about me.
tsw_comparator: When the Helper comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, that one will bear witness about me.
exact_source_record: ⸀Ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ παράκλητος ὃν ἐγὼ πέμψω ὑμῖν παρὰ τοῦ πατρός, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας ὃ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται, ἐκεῖνος μαρτυρήσει περὶ ἐμοῦ·

rationale: Keeps the disciples’ witness and its basis in continuous presence.
before: And you also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.”
after: And you also will testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.
tsw_comparator: And you also bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.
exact_source_record: καὶ ὑμεῖς δὲ μαρτυρεῖτε, ὅτι ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἐστε.

rationale: Preserves the preventive purpose and the image of stumbling into apostasy.
before: “I have told you these things so that you do not stumble.
after: “I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.
tsw_comparator: “These things I have spoken to you so that you may not stumble.
exact_source_record: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ σκανδαλισθῆτε.

rationale: Keeps synagogue exclusion, lethal persecution, future hour, and killers’ mistaken religious service.
before: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think they are offering service to God.
after: They will expel you from the synagogues. In fact, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think they are offering worship to God.
tsw_comparator: They will put you out of the synagogues; indeed, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he is offering service to God.
exact_source_record: ἀποσυναγώγους ποιήσουσιν ὑμᾶς· ἀλλʼ ἔρχεται ὥρα ἵνα πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας ὑμᾶς δόξῃ λατρείαν προσφέρειν τῷ θεῷ.

rationale: Preserves persecution’s stated cause and ignorance of both Father and Son.
before: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or me.
after: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or me.
tsw_comparator: And these things they will do because they have not known the Father nor me.
exact_source_record: καὶ ταῦτα ποιήσουσιν ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸν πατέρα οὐδὲ ἐμέ.

rationale: Keeps prediction, future remembrance, their appointed hour, and the reason for delayed warning.
before: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you. I did not tell you these things from the beginning because I was with you.
after: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you. I did not tell you these things from the beginning because I was with you.
tsw_comparator: But these things I have spoken to you so that when their hour comes you may remember that I told you of them. I did not say these things to you from the beginning, because I was with you.
exact_source_record: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἡ ὥρα ⸀αὐτῶν μνημονεύητε ⸁αὐτῶν ὅτι ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν. Ταῦτα δὲ ὑμῖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς οὐκ εἶπον, ὅτι μεθʼ ὑμῶν ἤμην.

rationale: Preserves return to the sender and Jesus’ observation despite earlier questions in another conversational moment.
before: “But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
after: But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
tsw_comparator: But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
exact_source_record: νῦν δὲ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐρωτᾷ με· Ποῦ ὑπάγεις;

rationale: Keeps contrast, cause, sorrow, fullness, and heart language.
before: Instead, because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your hearts.
after: Instead, because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your hearts.
tsw_comparator: But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
exact_source_record: ἀλλʼ ὅτι ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἡ λύπη πεπλήρωκεν ὑμῶν τὴν καρδίαν.

rationale: Preserves truth claim, advantage, necessary departure, Advocate, and Jesus’ sending.
before: But I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
after: Nevertheless, I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
tsw_comparator: But I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
exact_source_record: ἀλλʼ ἐγὼ τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω ὑμῖν, συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐγὼ ἀπέλθω. ἐὰν ⸀γὰρ μὴ ἀπέλθω, ὁ παράκλητος ⸂οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ⸃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐὰν δὲ πορευθῶ, πέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

rationale: Renders the verb’s range as expose and preserves the three subjects of the Spirit’s case against the world.
before: When he comes, he will expose the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment:
after: And when he comes, he will expose the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment:
tsw_comparator: And when that one comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment:
exact_source_record: καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐκεῖνος ἐλέγξει τὸν κόσμον περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ περὶ κρίσεως·

rationale: Keeps the explicit explanation linking sin and unbelief.
before: concerning sin, because they do not trust in me;
after: concerning sin, because they do not believe in me;
tsw_comparator: concerning sin, because they do not believe in me;
exact_source_record: περὶ ἁμαρτίας μέν, ὅτι οὐ πιστεύουσιν εἰς ἐμέ·

rationale: Preserves the stated reason, destination, and end of visible presence.
before: concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see me;
after: concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will see me no longer;
tsw_comparator: concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father and you no longer see me;
exact_source_record: περὶ δικαιοσύνης δέ, ὅτι πρὸς τὸν ⸀πατέρα ὑπάγω καὶ οὐκέτι θεωρεῖτέ με·

rationale: Keeps the completed judgment of the world’s ruler as the explanation.
before: concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
after: and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
tsw_comparator: concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
exact_source_record: περὶ δὲ κρίσεως, ὅτι ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου κέκριται.

rationale: Preserves remaining revelation and present inability to carry it.
before: “I still have many things to tell you, but you cannot bear them now.
after: I still have many things to tell you, but you cannot bear them now.
tsw_comparator: I still have many things to say to you, but you are not able to bear them now.
exact_source_record: Ἔτι πολλὰ ἔχω ⸂ὑμῖν λέγειν⸃, ἀλλʼ οὐ δύνασθε βαστάζειν ἄρτι·

rationale: Keeps personal agency, title, comprehensive guidance, dependent speech, hearing, and future disclosure.
before: When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you the things that are coming.
after: But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak on his own, but will speak whatever he hears, and he will announce to you what is to come.
tsw_comparator: But when that one comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth; for he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are coming.
exact_source_record: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς ⸂ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πάσῃ⸃, οὐ γὰρ λαλήσει ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ, ἀλλʼ ὅσα ⸀ἀκούσει λαλήσει, καὶ τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.

rationale: Preserves the Spirit’s glorifying work and reception and disclosure of what belongs to Jesus.
before: He will glorify me because he will take from what is mine and announce it to you.
after: He will glorify me because he will take what is mine and announce it to you.
tsw_comparator: That one will glorify me, because he will take from what is mine and will declare it to you.
exact_source_record: ἐκεῖνος ἐμὲ δοξάσει, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λήμψεται καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.

rationale: Keeps shared possession and the explanation of the preceding statement.
before: Everything the Father has is mine. This is why I said that he takes from what is mine and will announce it to you.
after: Everything the Father has is mine. That is why I said that the Spirit takes what is mine and will announce it to you.
tsw_comparator: All that the Father has is mine; therefore I said that he takes from what is mine and will declare it to you.
exact_source_record: πάντα ὅσα ἔχει ὁ πατὴρ ἐμά ἐστιν· διὰ τοῦτο εἶπον ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λαμβάνει καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.

rationale: Preserves the repeated short interval and contrasting sight.
before: “A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me.”
after: In a little while you will no longer see me, and then a little while later you will see me.”
tsw_comparator: A little while, and you no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me.”
exact_source_record: Μικρὸν καὶ ⸀οὐκέτι θεωρεῖτέ με, καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ ⸀με.

rationale: Keeps the disciples’ mutual question and both quoted sayings.
before: Some of his disciples said to one another, “What does he mean by saying, ‘A little while, and you will not see me, and again a little while, and you will see me,’ and, ‘because I am going to the Father’?”
after: Then some of his disciples said to one another, “What does he mean by telling us, ‘In a little while you will not see me, and then a little while later you will see me,’ and, ‘Because I am going to the Father’?
tsw_comparator: Therefore some of his disciples said to one another, “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you do not see me, and again a little while, and you will see me,’ and, ‘because I go to the Father’?”
exact_source_record: εἶπαν οὖν ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο ὃ λέγει ἡμῖν· Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με, καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με; καί· ⸀Ὅτι ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πατέρα;

rationale: Preserves their repeated question, focus on the phrase, and admitted ignorance.
before: They kept saying, “What is this ‘little while’ he speaks about? We do not know what he means.”
after: So they kept asking, “What does he mean by ‘a little while’? We do not know what he is talking about.”
tsw_comparator: So they were saying, “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what he is speaking about.”
exact_source_record: ἔλεγον οὖν· ⸂Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο⸃ ὃ ⸀λέγει μικρόν; οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί λαλεῖ.

rationale: Keeps Jesus’ knowledge, their desire, mutual discussion, and full repetition.
before: Jesus knew they wanted to ask him, so he said, “Are you discussing with one another what I meant when I said, ‘A little while, and you will not see me, and again a little while, and you will see me’?
after: Jesus knew that they wanted to question him, so he said to them, “Are you discussing with one another what I meant when I said, ‘In a little while you will not see me, and then a little while later you will see me’?
tsw_comparator: Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, “Are you discussing with one another this, that I said, ‘A little while, and you do not see me, and again a little while, and you will see me’?
exact_source_record: ⸀ἔγνω Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤθελον αὐτὸν ἐρωτᾶν, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Περὶ τούτου ζητεῖτε μετʼ ἀλλήλων ὅτι εἶπον· Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με, καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με;

rationale: Preserves double amen, contrasting responses, grief, and transformation into joy.
before: Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and mourn, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will become joy.
after: Truly, truly, I tell you: you will weep and mourn, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.
tsw_comparator: Truly, truly, I say to you, that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will become joy.
exact_source_record: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι κλαύσετε καὶ θρηνήσετε ὑμεῖς, ὁ δὲ κόσμος χαρήσεται· ⸀ὑμεῖς λυπηθήσεσθε, ἀλλʼ ἡ λύπη ὑμῶν εἰς χαρὰν γενήσεται.

rationale: Keeps the gender-specific embodied comparison, appointed hour, anguish, joy, birth, and world.
before: When a woman gives birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come. But when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the distress because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
after: When a woman is giving birth, she has pain because her hour has come. But when the child is born, she no longer remembers the anguish because of her joy that a human being has been born into the world.
tsw_comparator: When a woman is giving birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the distress, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
exact_source_record: ἡ γυνὴ ὅταν τίκτῃ λύπην ἔχει, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα αὐτῆς· ὅταν δὲ γεννήσῃ τὸ παιδίον, οὐκέτι μνημονεύει τῆς θλίψεως διὰ τὴν χαρὰν ὅτι ἐγεννήθη ἄνθρωπος εἰς τὸν κόσμον.

rationale: Preserves present sorrow, promised reunion, heart joy, and its security.
before: So you also have sorrow now, but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
after: So you also have sorrow now. But I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
tsw_comparator: So also you now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy from you.
exact_source_record: καὶ ὑμεῖς οὖν ⸂νῦν μὲν λύπην⸃ ἔχετε· πάλιν δὲ ὄψομαι ὑμᾶς, καὶ χαρήσεται ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία, καὶ τὴν χαρὰν ὑμῶν οὐδεὶς ⸀αἴρει ἀφʼ ὑμῶν.

rationale: Keeps the distinction between questioning Jesus and requesting from the Father, with double amen and Jesus’ name.
before: “On that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
after: On that day you will not ask me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
tsw_comparator: And in that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give to you.
exact_source_record: καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἐρωτήσετε οὐδέν· ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸂ἄν τι⸃ αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα ⸂δώσει ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου⸃.

rationale: Preserves the temporal contrast, command, promise, and fulfilled joy.
before: Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
after: Until now you have asked for nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
tsw_comparator: Until now you have asked nothing in my name; ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.
exact_source_record: ἕως ἄρτι οὐκ ᾐτήσατε οὐδὲν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου· αἰτεῖτε καὶ λήμψεσθε, ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν ᾖ πεπληρωμένη.

rationale: Keeps figurative speech, future hour, contrast, frankness, and subject.
